newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi to keep R&D at 17 pct of sales.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi to keep R&D at 17 pct of sales.

text.p: French health and beauty products group Sanofi said on Tuesday that it aimed to keep its spending on research and development at 17 percent of sales.

Chairman Jean-Francois Dehecq told an analysts' meeting that in case this spending had to rise, for a particular product with a high potential, Sanofi would seek an alliance with another drug group to spread out these costs.
"We have no intention to bring that (research spending) down. We will maintain our costs at 17 percent (of sales)," Dehecq said.
Sanofi will have 30 compounds in development programs at the beginning of 1997 and expects to file for a number of U.S. Food and Drug Administration approvals.
In September it filed in the U.S. and Europe for clopidogrel, a new platelet aggregation inhibitor that can be used to threat atherothrombosis more effectively than asperin.
The compound was jointly-developed with Bristol-Myers Squibb Corp and an application for approval will be filed in Japan in 1998.
Sanofi's Skelid, a bone-regulator which is already used in Paget's disease indications, will be the subject of filings for up to four new indications in 1997.
The company said that its portfolio of anti-cancer drugs alone -- Eloxatin, Zyrkamin, Tirazone and Utrate oxudase, had a sales potential of $250 million by the year 2000.
Other hopes for future drugs success include the synthetic pentasaccharide SR 90107, to be used during hip replacements.
In the area of central nervous system disorders Sanofi is testing the SR 57746 antineurodegeneretive agent in Amyothropic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and Alzheimer's disease.
Sanofi said that it expected full year 1996 pharmaceutical sales of 27.2 billion francs, including 9.7 billion for licensees.
Its key drug, the Ticlid oral antithrombotics product, will make up 4.6 billion of the amount and the Depakine antiepleptic 2.8 billion.
Sanofi is majority-owned by oil group Elf-Aquitaine
